summary: Ester Bianchi is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert, completing her PhD at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE. She held posts at the University of Perugia and Florence.
Ethan Tischler specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan University, earning his BA under advisor Mary-Jane Rubenstein as attested in 2014.
Etienne Vermeersch was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University from circa 1953 to 1965. He subsequently held a faculty post at Ghent University from 1967 to 1997.

Etsuaki Teraishi works in Indology and philosophy. Teraishi held an attested post as assistant professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College in 1999 and as a special researcher with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science in 2001.

Eugen Hultzsch was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig and under Georg Bühler in Vienna. He served as epigraphist for the Government of Madras and India (circa 1886–1903) and held a chair at Halle-Wittenberg from 1903 to 1925.

Eugen Pander was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied at Polytechnikum Riga. In 1881, he held an academic appointment at Tongwen Guan teaching economics, Russian, and German.
Eugen Prym was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1862 to 1868 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1870 until 1913.

Eugen Wilhelm was an Indologist and Iranian/Central Asian studies specialist who studied under August Schleicher from circa 1861 to 1865. He served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1869 to 1923.

Eugene Obermiller specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studying under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy from circa 1921 to 1925. He worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts and the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Eugene Watson Burlingame worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held academic posts at the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1910–1914), Johns Hopkins University (circa 1914–1917), and Yale University (circa 1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang is an art historian and scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield. He taught at the University of Chicago before becoming a professor at Harvard University.
Eugenio d'Ors was a philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona (circa 1897–1903) and Universidad Central (circa 1903–1905). He subsequently held an academic post at Universidad Central.
Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck was a linguist who studied at Leiden University from circa 1932 to 1939. He then served as a professor at Leiden University from 1950 to 1983.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (circa 1919–1924). He later held posts at Lviv, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, and the University of Warsaw (circa 1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian studies, studying under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served at the Société Asiatique and held a professorship at the Collège de France from 1832 to 1852.
Eugène Jacquet was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from circa 1829 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from circa 1832 to 1838.

Eugène Tisserant was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. His education included studies at Lycee Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert (circa 1896–1900), followed by the École du Louvre and INALCO between circa 1904 and 1908.
Eun Hino is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed a master's course at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and Musashino University.
Eun Maeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Kozui Otani. Maeda served as the president of both Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. She taught at the University of Michigan until 2004, when she joined Seoul National University.
